paragraphs.en: The presence of lens flares in images can significantly reduce the quality of downstream application results for tasks such as 3D scene reconstruction. This is because lens flares are a property of the camera imaging system, and not a part of the underlying scene being modeled. There are previous methods that tackle the removal of small flares focused around a light source. However, existing methods struggle with large flares, such as those that fill the entire image. In this work, we compile a novel dataset for large-flare removal, combining publicly available real-world data with a procedural generation pipeline. We fine-tune a diffusion-based model on our dataset to remove complex, large lens flares. On the other hand, lens flares remain effective artistic tools, widely used in the media. While there are ways to simulate 2D flares, representing and reconstructing lens flares consistently across multiple views has not yet been explored. To achieve this, we introduce a flare representation model that leverages the symmetry of lens flares about the camera’s principal point. We propose a computational pipeline to jointly optimize this flare model and a Gaussian splatting model (3DGS). This enables the decomposition of a 3D scene into lens flares and the scene itself, using our flare-removal model. Because the reconstructed flare is explicit and re-renderable, it can be edited and transferred to novel images and new 3D scenes. We evaluate removal on an established benchmark and a new one for large reflective flares, quantify the flare/scene decomposition directly, and show that the pipeline is robust to errors in automatic light-source localization.

paragraphs.en: Lens flares are artifacts caused by unintended light paths passing through the lens when a camera observes a sufficiently bright light source in the scene. In this work, we will refer to two subjective categories of lens flare appearance, see Fig. 2 . Scattering flares occur due to dust, lens defects, and scratches on lenses, causing lens glares, shimmer, and streaks in images, respectively. Reflective flares occur due to lens ensembles where lenses reflect a small percentage of the incident light.
paragraphs.zh: 当相机在场景中观测到足够明亮的光源时，由于光线意外地穿过镜头，会产生镜头眩光这种伪影。 在本研究中，我们将把镜头眩光的外观分为两类主观类别，参见图 2。 散射型眩光由镜头中的灰尘、镜头缺陷和划痕引起，分别会在图像中造成镜头眩光、闪烁和条纹。 反射型眩光则出现在镜头组中，此时镜头会反射入射光的一小部分。

paragraphs.en: In many downstream applications, it is important to remove lens flares. Existing flare removal methods ( Dai et al., 2023a ; Wu et al., 2021 ; Zhou et al., 2025 ) use real and synthetic lens flare datasets to add synthetic flares to images from a dataset without flares and learn to predict the original flare-free images. Such datasets are mainly composed of scattering flares. Although one dataset contains a few reflective flares, they cover a relatively small area and are not full-frame reflective flares. To augment these datasets, we compile a novel dataset with real-world large reflective flares and augment it with procedurally generated flares. As baselines, we train previously proposed models on our dataset for flare removal. Furthermore, we propose a novel approach that demonstrates that fine-tuning a diffusion model with LoRA for flare removal on these datasets yields better results, which also lead to better multi-view 3D reconstructions (Sec. 5.2 ). We evaluate all of the models on the scattering-flare-removal benchmark from Flare7K++ ( Dai et al., 2023a ) and propose a new benchmark for large reflective-flare removal. Further, we compile a dataset of 5 5 flare corrupted scenes to evaluate the performance of the flare-removal models across multiple views. We demonstrate that, on each benchmark, one of our two models outperforms all prior methods.

paragraphs.en: Lens flares are an important artistic tool in film, games, and virtual production, where they add cinematic realism and convey the presence of bright light sources. For downstream reconstruction tasks, although they are undesirable, understanding their effects and synthesizing them would help us better control the 3D reconstruction as lens flares are unavoidable in many situations. Existing flare simulators – stock compositing, procedural, and physically-based (Tab. 1 ) – can synthesize plausible flares, but none reconstruct the actual pattern of a given capture: physically-based methods only achieve viewpoint-correct appearance when the lens prescription is precisely known, diffractive effects, among the most distinctive aspects of lens flares, are computationally intractable to simulate at macroscopic lens scales, and modeling every possible real-world light source is not scalable. Our goal is instead to reconstruct the actual flare patterns present in captured footage, preserving lens- and capture-specific characteristics. For instance, in Fig. 3 , we see that the same lens leads to different types of lens flares with different light sources. Further, realistically editing lens flares into images requires extensive manual artistic effort. A view-consistent 3D flare representation is therefore valuable beyond removal: it enables reconstruction, and transfer of captured flares onto novel target images (see Fig. 1 ) and onto novel target scenes (see Fig. 14 ), none of which a per-image 2D removal model can provide.

paragraphs.en: Our goal is to enable reconstruction and real-time rendering of flares from any viewpoint. Reconstructing lens flares is inherently different from reconstructing a 3D scene, for instance, using Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). However, this does not hold for lens flares, which are not part of the 3D scene and change with the relative motion between the light sources and the camera, i.e., they are 3D inconsistent. Even deformable 3DGS methods assume that the underlying motion is 3D consistent and fail to reconstruct reflective lens flares. Hence, when we reconstruct a scene with images containing lens flares using 3DGS, the models either bake them into the 3D scene or ignore them altogether, as shown in Fig. 4 .

paragraphs.en: Therefore, we need a novel 3D representation that can reproduce the changing lens flare across different views. To achieve this, we model lens flares using Gaussians that are anchored to the camera on a near-plane in front of the scene, rather than as free-floating geometry in world space; this reflects the fact that flares are produced by the imaging system itself and move with the camera. Further, we design the flare representation model per light source based on the fact that lens flares approximately lie along the line joining the light source and the principal point in 2D ( Koreban and Schechner, 2009 ; Dai et al., 2023b ) . We constrain, by design, that all Gaussians lie on the projected 2D line connecting each light source to the camera’s principal point. We learn a deformation field to move and modulate lens flares based on the light and camera locations. We position the plane right after the near plane and rasterize it together with the scene in a single pass, so the flare adds little to rasterization cost and the full model still renders in real time. sents.en: We discuss existing methods for removing flares, followed by methods for 3D reconstruction.

paragraphs.en: FR ( Wu et al., 2021 ) is the pioneering work to train a UNet ( Ronneberger et al., 2015 ) to remove lens flares. Synthetic flares are added to a dataset of images, and the model is supervised with the flare-free images. Light sources are added to the generated flare-free images through threshold-based light detection. Later, many methods updated the model to UFormer ( Wang et al., 2022 ) , which remains the best performer across many datasets. Flare7K ( Dai et al., 2022 ) introduced a synthetic dataset composed of scattering and reflective flares, which helped improve the flare removal models greatly. Building on this method, Flare7K++ ( Dai et al., 2023a ) introduced a real scattering flares dataset, which further improved flare removal models. Along with the dataset, it also proposed a real-world benchmark for flare removal. However, this benchmark only tests for scattering flares and ignores lens glares, discussed later in the experiments section. BracketFlare ( Dai et al., 2023b ) is trained to remove a single small reflective flare that is symmetric around the principal point of the camera using synthetic data generation based on images captured using different exposures. On the other hand, DiffFlare ( Zhou et al., 2024 ) learns to guide a pretrained multi-step latent diffusion model for scattering flare removal. ACL-FR ( Zhou et al., 2023 ; Zhou et al., 2025 ) employs adversarial curve learning to model the image signal processing pipeline, thereby achieving improved flare removal for various camera types and enhanced preservation of lighting characteristics. FlareX ( Lishen et al., 2025 ) proposes a novel synthetic dataset for flare removal, including some large flares, which might benefit our model. LightsOut ( Tsai et al., 2025 ) proposes to outpaint an image to generate light sources for removing off-screen lens flares. Deng et al. ( Deng et al., 2024 ) estimate a flare-level map to guide blind flare removal, and Deflare-Net ( Ghodesawar et al., 2023 ) couples flare detection with removal; neither releases code or models, so we do not compare against them quantitatively. Contrary to existing methods, which focus on more exactly modeling the physics of flare corruption, we leverage a pretrained single-step diffusion model that enables fast flare removal by fine-tuning with LoRA ( Hu et al., 2022 ) on relatively small real data.
paragraphs.zh: FR（Wu 等人，2021）是训练 UNet（Ronneberger 等人，2015）以去除镜头眩光的开创性工作。 向图像数据集中添加合成眩光，并使用无眩光的图像对模型进行监督学习。 通过基于阈值的亮度检测，在生成的无眩光图像中添加光源。 随后，许多方法将模型更新为 UFormer（Wang 等人，2022），该模型在众多数据集中仍表现最佳。 Flare7K（Dai 等人，2022）引入了一个由散射眩光和反射眩光组成的合成数据集，极大地提升了眩光去除模型的性能。 基于此方法，Flare7K++（Dai 等人，2023a）引入了一个真实的散射眩光数据集，进一步改进了眩光去除模型。 除了数据集之外，该方法还提出了一项用于眩光去除的真实世界基准测试。 然而，该基准测试仅针对散射眩光进行检验，而忽略了镜头眩光，后者将在实验部分进一步讨论。 BracketFlare（Dai 等人，2023b）通过基于不同曝光图像的合成数据生成，训练模型以去除位于相机主点周围对称分布的单个小型反射眩光。 另一方面，DiffFlare（Zhou 等人，2024）学习引导一个预训练的多步潜在扩散模型，以实现散射眩光的去除。 ACL-FR（Zhou 等人，2023；Zhou 等人，2025）采用对抗性曲线学习来模拟图像信号处理流程，从而提升各类相机的眩光去除效果，并更好地保留光照特性。 FlareX（Lishen 等人，2025）提出了一种用于眩光去除的新合成数据集，其中包含一些较大的眩光，这或许能对我们的模型有所助益。 LightsOut（Tsai 等人，2025）提出通过图像外推生成光源，以去除画面外的镜头眩光。Deng 等人 （Deng 等人，2024）估计眩光水平图以指导盲态眩光去除，而 Deflare-Net（Ghodesawar 等人，2023）则将眩光检测与去除相结合；两者均未公开代码或模型，因此我们未对其进行量化比较。 与现有方法不同，后者更侧重于精确模拟眩光干扰的物理过程，而我们则利用一个预训练的单步扩散模型，通过基于 LoRA（Hu 等人，2022）在相对较小的真实数据上进行微调，实现快速眩光去除。

paragraphs.en: GN-FR ( Matta et al., 2024 ) is designed to remove small scattering flares from 3D scenes using a predicted flare mask. The idea is to completely ignore the regions with flares during the supervision of a generalizable NeRF 3D reconstruction model. Note that their data and code are not publicly released . The idea is built similarly to robust novel view synthesis methods ( Sabour et al., 2025 ; Zhu et al., 2023 ) , where distractors are detected and ignored. However, when the input contains large scattering or reflective flares, most of the information from these images is lost. We demonstrate the strength of our flare removal model in that it consistently removes flares across multi-view images without losing scene information. We also propose a novel benchmark for evaluating 3D reconstruction and novel-view synthesis under the presence of challenging scattering flares.
paragraphs.zh: GN-FR（Matta 等人，2024）旨在利用预测的耀斑掩码从三维场景中移除小型散射耀斑。 其核心思想是在通用 NeRF 三维重建模型的训练过程中完全忽略存在耀斑的区域。 请注意，他们的数据和代码尚未公开。 这一思路与稳健的新视角合成方法（Sabour 等人，2025；Zhu 等人，2023）类似，即检测并忽略干扰元素。 然而，当输入包含大型散射或反射耀斑时，这些图像中的大部分信息都会丢失。 我们证明了我们的耀斑移除模型的优势：它能在多视角图像中一致地移除耀斑，同时不丢失场景信息。 我们还提出了一种新的基准，用于评估在存在具有挑战性的散射耀斑情况下的三维重建和新视角合成能力。

paragraphs.en: Most existing methods ( Hullin et al., 2011 ; Maurer, 2024 ; Bodonyi and Kunkli, 2023 ; Bodonyi et al., 2025 ; Lee and Eisemann, 2013 ) model characteristics of specific lens ensembles for producing lens flares and focus on enabling real-time rendering of the modeled lens flares. Closer to our work, Koreban and Schechner ( Koreban and Schechner, 2009 ) analyze the geometric structure of aperture-ghost flares and show that, under lens rotational symmetry, ghost positions lie on the line connecting the light source projection and the optical center in the image plane. We exploit this same geometric property as a constraint inside a differentiable 3DGS pipeline.

paragraphs.en: Flare representation is a hard task, as lens flares, in general, are not 3D consistent. Therefore, existing 3D Gaussian splatting ( Kerbl et al., 2023 ) and even deformable 3DGS ( Luiten et al., 2024 ; Yang et al., 2023 ; Wu et al., 2024 ) reconstruction methods fail to represent lens flares, see Fig. 4 . However, it can be seen that scattering lens flares closer to the light source (in images) do not change significantly across views and are reconstructed near the light source in a 3D scene, even though they are not 3D-consistent. Yet, the models ignore reflective flares completely in the reconstructions and are heavily affected by scattering flares, as shown in Fig. 12 . Our proposed reconstruction pipeline, based on our flare representation model, decomposes and represents different kinds of lens flares.

paragraphs.en: In this work, we aim to develop a lens flare removal model and use it to learn a 3D representation of lens flares. We fine-tune a latent diffusion model as our flare removal model. We elaborate on it in the first part of this section.

paragraphs.en: To represent lens flares in 3D, we adopt a dynamic Gaussian splatting model, treating them as 3D Gaussians moving on a 2D plane. While rendering the scene, we place this 2D plane in front of the scene 3DGS and render the scene and the flares together.

paragraphs.en: Lens flares are primarily caused by unintended light paths passing through a lens when a camera observes a sufficiently bright light source. They are undesirable in many cases. Given the intractability of modeling the effects of different light sources on various lens types, we need a learning-based solution for lens flare removal. Most existing lens-flare removal models exclusively focus on scattering flares, small reflective flares, and shimmer.
paragraphs.zh: 当相机观测到足够明亮的光源时，意外穿过镜头的光路是造成镜头眩光的主要原因。 在许多情况下，这种现象是不理想的。 鉴于不同光源对各类镜头的影响难以建模，我们需要一种基于学习的方法来解决镜头眩光去除问题。 大多数现有的镜头眩光去除模型仅专注于散射型眩光、小型反射型眩光以及闪烁现象。

paragraphs.en: Following prior flare-removal work ( Wu et al., 2021 ; Dai et al., 2023a ) , we adopt the standard additive linear-radiance composition,
paragraphs.zh: 基于先前的耀斑去除研究（Wu 等人，2021；Dai 等人，2023a），我们采用了标准的加法线性辐射度组合方法，

paragraphs.en: where I scene I_{\text{scene}} is the underlying flare-free radiance, I flare I_{\text{flare}} is the additive flare contribution, and γ \gamma approximates an inverse camera response function (CRF). Eq. ( 1 ) is exact under a monotone, non-saturating CRF; known deviations – highlight clipping, ISP non-linearities, and veiling glare – are inherited by all existing flare-removal baselines. Capturing per-pixel-paired real flare and flare-free images is impractical at scale, since it would require two perfectly co-located cameras with and without flare contributions. Hence, we (like prior work) train on synthetic composites obtained by blending real flare layers onto clean images using Eq. ( 1 ), inheriting the additivity assumption. The additive model is used only for this synthesis; it plays no role in the 3D flare representation.
paragraphs.zh: 其中，I scene I_{\text{scene}} 是底层无耀斑的辐射亮度，I flare I_{\text{flare}} 是叠加的耀斑贡献项，而 γ \gamma 近似表示一个反向相机响应函数（CRF）。在单调且非饱和的 CRF 条件下，公式 (1) 是精确的；但已知的一些偏差——例如高光截断、ISP 非线性以及漫反射眩光——会被所有现有的耀斑去除基线方法所继承。大规模捕捉每像素成对的真实耀斑图像和无耀斑图像是不切实际的，因为这需要两台位置完全重合的相机：一台包含耀斑贡献，另一台则不包含。因此，我们（与先前的研究一样）使用公式 (1) 将真实耀斑层叠加到干净图像上，从而生成合成图像进行训练，并由此继承了可加性假设。该可加模型仅用于这种合成过程，在 3D 耀斑表示中并不发挥作用。

paragraphs.en: We introduce a unified flare removal model that works with different types of lens flares - scattering, and reflective (both full image and small). We fine-tune a latent diffusion model for this task. Specifically, we adopt the diffusion model in Difix3D+ ( Wu et al., 2025 ) . The model is trained on a dataset of billions of images, making it well-suited for generating flare-free images. Furthermore, the fine-tuning paradigm in Difix3D+, based on single-step image-to-image translation models, is ideally suited to our task.

paragraphs.en: Representing lens flares using physically based models across different lens types is challenging, as different lens ensembles produce distinct flares under varying light sources, necessitating accurate physical models of those sources in real-world scenes. Further, accurately modeling the effect of the lenses requires not only precise prescriptions for all lens elements but also modeling of coherent propagation effects at the wavelength scale to precisely reproduce lens flares, with corresponding geometric detail for all components in the lens, particularly parts like iris blades that produce diffraction. Therefore, we adopt Gaussian splatting to represent and reconstruct lens flares in a given scene.

paragraphs.en: Our goal is to represent lens flares with minimum overhead over the scene representation - 3DGS. Therefore, we use 3D Gaussians as the final output of our lens flare representation, allowing us to rasterize the scene along with the lens flare effects. In 3DGS ( Kerbl et al., 2023 ) , the scene is modeled as a collection of 3D Gaussians 𝒢 \mathcal{G} , endowed with a mean μ \mu , scale s s , covariance Σ \Sigma , opacity σ \sigma , and color as spherical harmonics with b b -bases s ​ h sh ; 𝒢 = { μ , s , Σ , σ , s ​ h } \mathcal{G}=\{\mu,s,\Sigma,\sigma,sh\} . The Gaussians are initialized with a point cloud from Colmap ( Schönberger et al., 2016 ; Schönberger and Frahm, 2016 ) . The Gaussians are rasterized to input camera locations, and the parameters are optimized using a loss function that compares the input images with the rasterized images. We refer the readers to 3DGS ( Kerbl et al., 2023 ) for a more elaborate explanation.

paragraphs.en: Our representation places flares on the image-plane line through the principal point p p and the projected light location l l ( Koreban and Schechner, 2009 ; Dai et al., 2023b ) , and parameterizes each flare component by its radial position along that line. Concretely, each flare component is a set of canonical 1D Gaussians whose scalar mean μ ∈ ℝ \mu\in\mathbb{R} encodes radial offset. A small MLP, conditioned on the camera and light positions, deforms these canonical Gaussians; the deformed scalar mean μ ′ \mu^{\prime} is then (i) lifted to a 2D image point via μ ′ ​ ( ( l + δ l ) − p ) + p \mu^{\prime}\big((l+\delta_{l})-p\big)+p , (ii) unprojected to a depth equal to the near plane + ϵ +\epsilon in the camera frame, and (iii) emitted as a standard 3DGS primitive (Fig. 7 ). Because the entire construction lives in the camera frame and produces standard 3DGS primitives, the scene rasterizer is reused unchanged, and the flare component is rigidly tied to the camera, independent of the scene geometry behind it. The remainder of this section details the parameterization, deformation MLP, and light-position correction.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的表示方法将耀斑置于通过主点 p p 和投影光点位置 l l 的图像平面直线上（Koreban 和 Schechner，2009；Dai 等，2023b），并通过该直线上的径向位置对每个耀斑组件进行参数化。 具体来说，每个耀斑组件是一组规范的一维高斯函数，其标量均值 μ ∈ ℝ \mu\in\mathbb{R} 编码了径向偏移。 一个小型 MLP 以相机和光点位置为条件对这些规范高斯函数进行形变；随后，形变后的标量均值 μ ′ \mu^{\prime} 会（i）通过 μ ′ ​ ( ( l + δ l ) − p ) + p \mu^{\prime}\big((l+\delta_{l})-p\big)+p 提升至二维图像点，（ii）反投影到相机坐标系中距离近平面 + ϵ +\epsilon 的深度处，并（iii）作为标准的 3DGS 原始体发射出来（图 7）。 由于整个构建过程都在相机坐标系中进行，并且生成的是标准的 3DGS 原始体，因此场景光栅化器可以原样复用，而耀斑组件则与相机刚性绑定，独立于其背后的场景几何结构。 本节的其余部分将详细说明参数化方法、形变 MLP 以及光点位置校正。

paragraphs.en: Our lens flare model is inspired by the Deformable 3DGS ( Yang et al., 2023 ) (Def-3DGS). Our model features a set of canonical Gaussians representing lens flares, along with a deformation model that deforms them based on the light location and camera position. Unlike in Def-3DGS, however, the Gaussians in our lens flare model are one-dimensional ( μ ∈ ℝ 1 \mu\in\mathbb{R}^{1} , with a slight abuse of notation), as the location of the lens flares is generally restricted to the line connecting the principal point to the 2D position of the light source in image space ( Koreban and Schechner, 2009 ; Dai et al., 2023b ) . While Def-3DGS models condition on time, we condition our deformation model on the camera and light locations to modulate the canonical flare Gaussians, since lens flares depend on the relative positions of the camera and light.

paragraphs.en: In an ideal lens-flare model, every Gaussian in the scene contributes to the lens flares and is attenuated proportionally to its intensity. However, even with reliable Gaussian intensities, instantiating the ideal flare model for every Gaussian in the scene – rather than for a small, sparse set of discrete emitters – is computationally wasteful. Further, an ideal camera sensor that captures the full dynamic range would make it trivial to identify light sources directly from the Gaussians themselves, e.g., by thresholding on intensity. But captured images have limited dynamic range, so the intensities recovered by a 3DGS reconstruction are an unreliable proxy for true radiance. Light sources are precisely the regions most prone to over-exposure and clipping.

paragraphs.en: We obtain locations and the number of light sources using Grounded-SAM2 ( Ren et al., 2024 ) and TRASE ( Li et al., 2026 ) . Grounded-SAM2 has two stages: GroundingDINO ( Liu et al., 2023 ) produces bounding boxes, which are then input to SAM2 ( Ravi et al., 2024 ) for masks. We first obtain all bounding-box detections for the text prompt, “light source”, from GroundingDINO, and pass them to SAM2 to obtain a mask per box. We then apply two refinement steps to suppress spurious detections. First, since light sources are typically over-exposed, we discard any detection whose mask is not over-exposed, i.e. whose mean brightness (the HSV value channel) falls below 190 190 out of 255 255 ; this removes detections on non-emissive objects. Second, when multiple bounding boxes overlap on the same source (high intersection relative to the smaller box, or one box contained in another), we keep the box with the smallest area, as it most tightly localizes the emitter and avoids region-level boxes that merge a source with its surroundings. We measure the reliability of Grounded-SAM2 in the supplemental Sec. A.3.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用 Grounded-SAM2（Ren 等人，2024）和 TRASE（Li 等人，2026）获取光源的位置和数量。 Grounded-SAM2 包含两个阶段：GroundingDINO（Liu 等人，2023）生成边界框，随后将这些边界框输入 SAM2（Ravi 等人，2024）以获取掩码。 我们首先从 GroundingDINO 获取文本提示“light source”的所有边界框检测结果，并将其传入 SAM2，为每个边界框生成一个掩码。 接着，我们应用两个优化步骤来抑制虚假检测。 首先，由于光源通常过曝，我们会丢弃任何掩码未过曝的检测结果，即其平均亮度（HSV 值通道）低于 190/255；这可以排除非发光物体上的检测结果。 其次，当多个边界框重叠在同一个光源上时（交叠区域相对于较小的边界框较大，或一个边界框完全包含在另一个中），我们会保留面积最小的边界框，因为它能最精确地定位发光体，并避免将光源与其周围环境合并的区域级边界框。 我们在补充材料的 A.3 节中评估了 Grounded-SAM2 的可靠性。

paragraphs.en: We train our flare removal model with the Flare7k++ ( Dai et al., 2023a ) and the Flickr24K ( Zhang et al., 2018 ) datasets. However, the flare dataset is limited to small reflective flares. Therefore, we compile a large reflective flares dataset from publicly available real visual effects videos of large flares ( ActionVFX, 2026 ) . We obtain 1866 1866 training images from 90 90 clips spanning three effect categories (halo, icon and shimmer), and hold out 18 18 further clips entirely for testing, so that no test flare shares a source clip with any training flare. We compile the VFX benchmark by compositing flares from these held-out clips onto 128 128 images from our captures.

paragraphs.en: To quantify the differences between Flare7K++’s and our VFX flares, we measure, for each isolated flare layer, the fraction of the frame that contains 90 % 90\% of the flare’s energy, a threshold- and resolution-independent measure of spatial extent. Flare7K++’s reflective flares have a median coverage of 0.39 % 0.39\% (interquartile range (IQR) 0.13 0.13 – 1.81 % 1.81\% , N = 2000 N=2000 ), whereas the flares in our VFX dataset have a median of 78.0 % 78.0\% (IQR 69.1 69.1 – 82.5 % 82.5\% , N = 1866 N=1866 ); the IQRs do not overlap. Large full-frame reflective flares are therefore absent from existing data rather than merely under-represented. The two sets also differ in provenance. Flare7K++’s reflective flares are synthetic, generated from 10 10 base patterns; its real world subset, captured on the rear cameras of three smartphones, contains scattering flares only ( Dai et al., 2023a ) . paragraphs.en: We capture 9 9 diverse scenes spanning a mix of indoor and outdoor settings, multiple lens types (varying in focal length and ensemble), and a variety of real-world light sources – an LED headlamp, workshop lighting, a smartphone flashlight, a street lamp, and a purple-hued decorative light – so as to elicit a broad range of reflective flare patterns. We capture ∼ 1 \sim 1 min sequences, use 300 300 – 400 400 evenly spaced video frames for training, and 40 40 images from the remaining frames for testing. Held-out views far from the training trajectory are impractical here: we captured each sequence only for as long as the flare remained visible, so camera motion was bounded by the point at which the light left the frame and the flare vanished, rather than by any preference for a narrow sweep. These held-out frames are therefore interleaved with the training frames, so they test interpolation between nearby viewpoints within that range; extrapolation to new viewpoints and scenes is shown through transfer (Sec. 5.4 ) and in the supplementary webpage. Unlike ordinary scene content, flare appearance is governed by the light’s position relative to the optical axis rather than by scene-point parallax, and this mapping is highly nonlinear: small camera or light motions can produce disproportionately large changes in ghost position, halo extent, and streak orientation (Sec. 5.5 ). Interpolating this deformation between nearby frames is therefore non-trivial. Unlike the 5 5 -scene removal dataset above, a per-pixel ground-truth flare-free image and flare layer are intractable to obtain in real captures, since the scene and flare radiance are entangled at the sensor; separating them optically would require specialized capture hardware that is impractical for handheld video. We therefore evaluate decomposition against a model-derived reference, which we define and justify in Sec. 5.3 .

paragraphs.en: In this section, we evaluate the performance of our lens flare removal model. First, we compare our model against established baselines on the Flare7K++ ( Dai et al., 2023a ) benchmark for scattering flare removal. Then, we compare our model against baselines on our proposed VFX benchmark. One of the most significant benefits of our method is that it requires only 20 20 hours to fine-tune our model (on a single GPU), whereas our baselines take more than 4 4 days to train.
paragraphs.zh: 在本节中，我们评估了镜头眩光去除模型的性能。 首先，我们在 Flare7K++（Dai et al., 2023a）基准数据集上，将我们的模型与现有的基准模型进行了散射眩光去除能力的对比。 接着，我们在我们提出的 VFX 基准数据集上，将我们的模型与基准模型进行了对比。 我们方法最显著的优势之一是，只需 20 小时即可对模型进行微调（使用单 GPU），而我们的基准模型则需要超过 4 天才能完成训练。

sents.en: First, we compare our model against established baselines on the Flare7K++ ( Dai et al., 2023a ) benchmark for scattering flare removal.

paragraphs.en: The Flare7K++ benchmark mainly evaluates scattering flare removal. We compare our model with the top-performing scattering-flare-removal models: Flare7K++ ( Dai et al., 2023a ) , FR ( Wu et al., 2021 ) , and ACL-FR ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) by retraining the models with our VFX dataset and procedural flares in addition to the Flare7K++ dataset. Further, we compare with the released versions of LightsOut ( Tsai et al., 2025 ) and FlareX ( Lishen et al., 2025 ) ; note that LightsOut is designed to outpaint off-screen light sources ahead of an existing removal network, whereas we evaluate it as a standalone remover. Quantitative results for the comparison are shown in Tab. 2 . As shown, our model, which incorporates supervision of light sources and lens glare, outperforms all existing models on the benchmark, which also contains lens glare. paragraphs.en: We evaluate our design choices of our flare removal model qualitatively in Fig. 11 , and quantitatively in Tab. 2 . One key design choice is to incorporate light sources into the supervision images, eliminating the need for a post-processing step to add light back to the flare-removed images, as in our baselines. We demonstrate this in ‘wo light’, where we train the model to remove light sources and then add them back as a post-processing step. While baseline models, especially Flare7K++ ( Dai et al., 2023a ) , perform well when a light source is added back to the images, we observed that our diffusion-based model does not perform as well on either benchmark (Tab. 2 , ‘wo light’). Another important design choice is to fine-tune the VAE encoder with LoRA. We demonstrate the importance of this in ‘wo enc FT’, where we do not fine-tune the VAE encoder. Quantitatively, our models outperform the model without encoder finetuning. paragraphs.en: The target is not self-evident. A light source is a genuine scene emitter, yet the glare surrounding it is produced by the imaging system, so the boundary between ‘scene’ and ‘flare’ has to be stated rather than assumed. We settle it by choice of reference. Taking I removed I_{\text{removed}} , the output of our removal model Ours, as the flare-free reference, we require (i) the scene render to match I removed I_{\text{removed}} , and (ii) the flare branch’s contribution to match the residual I input − I removed I_{\text{input}}-I_{\text{removed}} . Because Ours retains the light source while removing the flare and the glare around it (Sec. 3.1 ), the emitter falls on the scene side and the artifacts it induces on the flare side. This reference measures the contribution of flares to the composite scene rather than the flare itself. We need this difference-based reference because rendering the flare Gaussians alone would composite them against an empty background, and we have no direct reference against which to evaluate such a render. We therefore compute the flare contribution as | I scene+flare − I scene | |I_{\text{scene+flare}}-I_{\text{scene}}| . Both sides of (ii) are thus formed alike, which makes the criterion agnostic to the compositing strategy.
paragraphs.zh: 目标并非不言自明的。 光源是真实的场景发射体，但围绕其产生的眩光是由成像系统生成的，因此“场景”与“光晕”之间的边界必须明确说明，而非默认假设。 我们通过选择参考来界定这一边界。 将 I removed I_{\text{removed}}（即我们移除模型 Ours 的输出）作为无光晕的参考，我们需要满足两个条件：(i) 场景渲染结果与 I removed I_{\text{removed}} 一致；(ii) 光晕分支的贡献与残差 I input − I removed I_{\text{input}}-I_{\text{removed}} 一致。 由于 Ours 在移除光晕及其周围眩光的同时保留了光源（第 3.1 节），因此发射体属于场景部分，而它引发的伪影则属于光晕部分。 该参考衡量的是光晕对合成场景的贡献，而非光晕本身。 我们需要这种基于差异的参考，因为单独渲染光晕高斯函数会将其与空背景进行合成，而我们没有直接的参考来评估这样的渲染结果。 因此，我们将光晕贡献计算为 | I scene+flare − I scene | |I_{\text{scene+flare}}-I_{\text{scene}}|。 这样，(ii) 中的两个部分都以相同方式构成，使得该标准与合成策略无关。

paragraphs.en: The residual in (ii) is not a pure flare layer. A flare saturates and occludes the scene behind it, so no exact flare is recoverable from a single image, and I input − I removed I_{\text{input}}-I_{\text{removed}} therefore also absorbs the discrepancy between the true occluded content and Ours’s reconstruction of it, including any light-source energy the removal model does not reproduce exactly. The flare branch is trained to account for whatever the removal model does not, so the two components together reconstruct the input regardless of where the removal model draws its boundary. Because flare Gaussians are composited in front of the scene, a transferred flare also carries its own light source into a new target (Fig. 1 ). It remains a close proxy for flare reconstruction quality, because reproducing the flare’s contribution to the composite is exactly what our flare branch is responsible for. As I removed I_{\text{removed}} is model-derived, the scene and flare metrics measure agreement with this reference rather than with an unobtainable ground truth: they are meaningful for comparing variants scored against a common reference, but not as absolute quality figures. Two facts limit this circularity: all metrics are computed at held-out frames that no model sees during training, and Ours was never trained on these scenes; it is validated separately on real paired captures (Flare7K++, Tab. 2 ) and, across views, by reconstructions that best match real flare-free captures (Sec. 5.2 ). What remains is shared bias: variants supervised with I removed I_{\text{removed}} inherit its systematic errors, which the reference also carries, so their scores are modestly favoured over variants that are not. Only the composite render is compared to the captured image directly, making it the sole removal-independent measure.

paragraphs.en: The results in Fig. 13 demonstrate that 3DGS initialized with Colmap ( Schönberger et al., 2016 ; Schönberger and Frahm, 2016 ) can reconstruct some scattering flares close to the light source that are approximately 3D consistent, as Colmap provides some initialization for these flares. However, reflective flares in the given images are completely ignored, as they are highly variable in shape, color, and size across views, and Colmap cannot provide initializations for such 3D inconsistent objects. Our model, ‘Ours’, on the other hand, helps reconstruct the highly variable flare objects and represents them consistently across different views (see supplementary video for flares rendered from novel views). On the composite Scene & Flare metric our model exceeds vanilla 3DGS by only 0.69 0.69 dB; this is expected, since both are fit to the same captured images and flare-affected pixels are a limited fraction of each frame, so even a model that smears or ignores the flare scores well on a whole-image metric. The two differ on decomposition (Tab. 4 , Fig. 13 ), where vanilla 3DGS produces no flare component at all and cannot be scored – whole-image metrics measure reconstruction quality rather than decomposition, so composite fidelity is a sanity check here, not the axis of comparison.
paragraphs.zh: 图 13 中的结果表明，使用 Colmap（Schönberger et al., 2016；Schönberger and Frahm, 2016）初始化的 3DGS 能够重建靠近光源的部分散射耀斑，这些耀斑在三维上大致一致，因为 Colmap 为这些耀斑提供了一定的初始化信息。 然而，给定图像中的反射耀斑被完全忽略了，因为它们在形状、颜色和大小上在不同视角间变化极大，而 Colmap 无法为这类三维不一致的物体提供初始化信息。 另一方面，我们的模型“Ours”有助于重建这些变化极大的耀斑物体，并在不同视角间以一致的方式呈现它们（请参见补充视频，其中展示了从新视角渲染的耀斑）。 在复合场景与耀斑指标上，我们的模型仅比基础 3DGS 高出 0.69 dB；这是可以预见的，因为两者都是基于相同的采集图像进行拟合的，而受耀斑影响的像素在每帧中仅占很小一部分，因此即使一个模型对耀斑进行了模糊处理或完全忽略，它在整张图像的指标上仍能获得不错的分数。 两者在分解结果上存在差异（表 4、图 13）：基础 3DGS 完全没有生成耀斑成分，因此无法评分——整张图像指标衡量的是重建质量而非分解效果，所以这里的复合保真度仅用于验证合理性，而非比较的核心维度。

paragraphs.en: Our representation renders in real time at capture resolution. Flare Gaussians are emitted as standard 3DGS primitives and concatenated with the scene Gaussians for a single rasterization pass, so no additional render is required. Measured on an RTX 4090 at × 1080 1920\!\times\!1080 on a single-light scene ( hat ; 10,965 10{,}965 flare Gaussians alongside 162,283 162{,}283 scene Gaussians), the deformation pass takes 3.92 3.92 ms and the joint rasterization of all 173,248 173{,}248 Gaussians takes 6.86 6.86 ms, for a frame time of 10.79 10.79 ms ( 92.7 92.7 FPS). Rasterizing the scene alone – vanilla 3DGS on the same scene – takes 6.74 6.74 ms ( 148 148 FPS), so batching the flare Gaussians into the same pass adds only 1.8 % 1.8\% to rasterization cost; the deformation pass is the dominant expense of the flare model. It evaluates per Gaussian rather than per pixel, and we measure it to be independent of output resolution. We instantiate one flare model per light source, each with its own deformation network and canonical Gaussians, so this cost grows with the number of lights: 3.9 3.9 , 6.8 6.8 , and 11.1 11.1 ms for one, two, and three lights.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的表示方法能够以采集分辨率实时渲染。 耀斑高斯函数作为标准的 3DGS 原语被发射出来，并与场景高斯函数拼接，从而只需一次光栅化操作，因此无需额外的渲染。 在 RTX 4090 上，于 ×1080 1920\!\times\!1080 分辨率下对单光源场景（包含 10,965 个耀斑高斯函数和 162,283 个场景高斯函数）进行测量时，形变步骤耗时 3.92 ms，所有 173,248 个高斯函数的联合光栅化耗时 6.86 ms，总帧时间为 10.79 ms（即 92.7 FPS）。 仅对场景进行光栅化——即在同一场景上使用基础版 3DGS——需要 6.74 ms（即 148 FPS），因此将耀斑高斯函数批处理到同一操作中，只会使光栅化成本增加 1.8%；形变步骤是耀斑模型的主要开销。 该评估以每个高斯函数为单位进行，而非每个像素，且经测量确认其结果与输出分辨率无关。 我们为每个光源实例化一个耀斑模型，每个模型都拥有独立的形变网络和标准高斯函数，因此该成本会随光源数量的增加而增长：一个、两个和三个光源时，耗时分别为 3.9 ms、6.8 ms 和 11.1 ms。

paragraphs.en: Our goals for the flare removal model are to decompose the input images to have a good 3D scene reconstruction alongside lens flares that can generalize to novel views. We perform ablations on our flare representation model to evaluate our design choices towards these goals. We show qualitative results in Fig. 13 , and quantitative results in Tab. 4 . In ‘Ours 2D’, we allow the flare Gaussians to move freely in the 2D plane, without our 1D representation. This model struggles to reconstruct flares since the Gaussians are unconstrained (flare PSNR 27.77 27.77 dB vs. 33.27 33.27 dB for Ours), and the composite reconstruction degrades correspondingly (Scene+Flare PSNR 27.76 27.76 dB, the lowest of all ablations). Next, we evaluate the effect of scene supervision on decomposition. In ‘Ours sup in-Flare’ and ‘Ours unsup’, we train the scene Gaussians with the reconstructed flare image subtracted from the input image and with no scene-only supervision, respectively. These models lead to inconsistent decompositions, missing different aspects of flares inconsistently across different scenes. However, ‘Ours unsup’, whose flare model augments 3DGS in reconstructing aspects of the captures that 3DGS misses, namely reflective lens flares, attains the highest composite PSNR of all variants. In ‘Ours wo δ l \delta_{l} ’, we train our model without the light position correction in Eq. ( 6 ). It performs on par with ‘Ours’, as the finer deformations δ f \delta_{f} absorb the light-position error (Sec. 5.5 ). Further, in ‘Ours wo G-SAM2’, we initialize the light source locations using the centroid of the scene’s Colmap point cloud with added noise, demonstrating that our model can fairly accurately reconstruct flares even without explicit light source detection, thanks to the light-position correction and finer deformations (Eq. ( 6 ), Eq. ( 5 )). In ‘Ours wo δ f \delta_{f} ’, where we train the model without the finer deformations δ f \delta_{f} (see Eq. ( 5 )), the model struggles to reconstruct asymmetric flares, leading to a slightly lower performance on flare reconstruction (PSNR of 32.99 32.99 dB). While the ‘Ours unsup’ achieves higher composite Scene+Flare PSNR ( 33.67 33.67 vs. 33.06 33.06 dB for Ours)—since the flare model’s additional capacity improves overall reconstruction—it performs poorly on scene decomposition ( 20.97 20.97 vs. 31.79 31.79 dB for Ours).
paragraphs.zh: 我们对耀斑移除模型的目标是，将输入图像进行分解，以实现良好的三维场景重建，同时保留能够泛化到新视角的镜头耀斑。我们对耀斑表示模型进行了消融实验，以评估为实现这些目标而做出的设计选择。我们在图13中展示了定性结果，并在表4中展示了定量结果。在“Ours 2D”中，我们允许耀斑高斯函数在二维平面上自由移动，而没有使用我们的二维表示方法。由于高斯函数不受约束，该模型难以重建耀斑（耀斑PSNR为27.77 dB，而“Ours”模型为33.27 dB），其组合重建效果也相应下降（场景+耀斑PSNR为27.76 dB，是所有消融实验中最低的）。接下来，我们评估了场景监督对分解过程的影响。在“Ours sup in-Flare”和“Ours unsup”中，我们分别使用从输入图像中减去重建耀斑图像后的结果来训练场景高斯函数，以及完全不进行场景单独监督的方式。这些模型导致了不一致的分解结果，在不同场景中遗漏了耀斑的不同方面。然而，“Ours unsup”的耀斑模型通过增强3DGS，重建了3DGS未能捕捉到的内容（即反射性镜头耀斑），因此在所有变体中获得了最高的组合PSNR。在“Ours wo δ l \delta_{l} ’中，我们在训练时未使用公式(6)中的光位置校正。其表现与“Ours”相当，因为更精细的形变δ f \delta_{f}吸收了光位置误差（见第5.5节）。此外，在“Ours wo G-SAM2”中，我们使用带有噪声的场景Colmap点云的质心来初始化光源位置，结果表明，得益于光位置校正和更精细的形变（公式(6)、公式(5)），即使没有明确的光源检测，我们的模型也能相当准确地重建耀斑。在“Ours wo δ f \delta_{f} ’中，我们在训练时未使用更精细的形变δ f \delta_{f}（见公式(5)），导致模型难以重建非对称耀斑，从而使得耀斑重建性能略有下降（PSNR为32.99 dB）。尽管“Ours unsup”实现了更高的场景+耀斑组合PSNR（33.67 dB，而“Ours”为33.06 dB）——因为耀斑模型增加的容量提升了整体重建效果——但它在场景分解方面的表现却较差（20.97 dB，而“Ours”为31.79 dB）。

paragraphs.en: Our model achieves the best flare decomposition (PSNR 33.27 33.27 dB) while remaining within 0.1 0.1 dB of the highest scene-decomposition PSNR ( 31.89 31.89 for ‘Ours wo G-SAM2’ vs. 31.79 31.79 dB for ‘Ours’). However, Ours outperforms ‘Ours wo G-SAM2’ in Flare decomposition reconstruction by ∼ 1.1 \sim 1.1 dB PSNR. Our model therefore offers the best scene/flare separation, which is the desired trade-off for our decomposable-reconstruction goal.

paragraphs.en: The ablations above are not only design controls; each also corresponds to a useful operating point of our framework. The default Ours setting bundles the light source and its flare into a single, self-contained 3D flare effect, suitable for transferring the captured flare to other scenes (e.g., VFX). Ours unsup instead prioritizes faithful composite reconstruction with flares, giving the highest Scene+Flare PSNR ( 33.67 33.67 , vs. 33.06 33.06 dB for the default), and serves applications that need flare-preserving re-rendering. The user can thus pick the training configuration matching the downstream task.

paragraphs.en: We first demonstrate transfer onto a target that has no associated 3D reconstruction at all: an arbitrary 2D target image (Fig. 1 ). Because such a target carries no camera pose, scene geometry, or light-source depth, the camera- and light-conditioned anchoring used for scene transfer (below) does not apply. Instead, we specify a single 2D point in the target image as the desired light-source location – either manually or via the same Grounded-SAM2 detection used elsewhere in our pipeline – and query the flare MLP with the source camera and source light as before, so the transferred flare keeps its learned in-distribution shape and color, while its placement is now driven by this target-image point rather than a projected 3D light position. The resulting flare Gaussians are rendered and alpha-composited directly onto the target image. As the target image carries no depth information, we do not perform a visibility test in this setting: the flare is composited unconditionally on top of the target image.

paragraphs.en: To demonstrate that our learned flares are not tied to the scene they were optimized on, we transfer flares trained on three source scenes – two from our captured reconstruction dataset (Sec. 5.3 ) and one additional captured scene not part of either dataset (also used for source flares in Fig. 1 ) – onto a single target scene that likewise does not appear in either of our captured datasets (Sec. 4 ) and is used only as a transfer target (Fig. 14 ). Both of these additional captures use the sun as the light source, diversifying beyond the light types in Sec. 5.3 . Each flare MLP ensemble is optimized jointly with its source scene’s Gaussians and is conditioned on the source cameras and light positions. At transfer time we decouple appearance from placement . The MLP is conditioned on camera and light positions and can be queried at any of them, as the supplementary video shows by sweeping the light along the principal-point line and then moving the camera as well. For transfer, however, we deliberately query it with the source camera and the source light it was trained with, since a target camera may lie well outside the source capture’s distribution and would elicit an extrapolated flare. This keeps the learned flare shape and color in-distribution, while the resulting flare Gaussians are anchored to the target scene by placing them relative to the target camera and aiming them at the target scene’s light position(s). For each frame we first rasterize the target Gaussians from the target camera, which also yields an inverse-depth map used for a per-light visibility test: a flare is instantiated only for target lights that are not occluded by target geometry. One flare is built per visible target light and the instances are merged, then composited with the target render so that the transferred flare correctly blends with (and is occluded by) the target scene. Because the flare follows the target cameras, we render along the target scene’s smooth video trajectory to produce the transfer sequences. Since the flare is represented explicitly as Gaussians, it also remains directly editable after transfer: the bottom row of Fig. 14 shows a transferred flare with its Gaussians uniformly scaled by 2 × 2\times , giving simple artistic control over the flare’s apparent intensity and extent without any retraining.
paragraphs.zh: 为了证明我们学到的光晕效果并不局限于其优化时所基于的场景，我们将基于三个源场景训练的光晕效果迁移到一个单一的目标场景中——这三个源场景包括两个来自我们采集的重建数据集（第 5.3 节）的场景，以及一个未包含在任何数据集中的额外采集场景（该场景也用于图 1 中的源光晕效果）；而目标场景同样未出现在我们的任何采集数据集中（第 4 节），且仅用作迁移目标（图 14）。 这两个额外的采集场景均以太阳为光源，从而超越了第 5.3 节中提到的光照类型。 每个光晕 MLP 集成模型都与源场景的高斯函数一同进行联合优化，并以源相机和光源位置为条件。 在迁移时，我们将外观与位置解耦。 MLP 以相机和光源位置为条件，并可在任意位置进行查询；补充视频通过沿主点线移动光源，随后再移动相机来展示了这一点。 然而，在迁移过程中，我们故意使用其训练时所依赖的源相机和源光源进行查询，因为目标相机可能完全位于源采集数据的分布范围之外，从而引发外推式的光晕效果。 这样既能保持所学光晕的形状和颜色处于数据分布范围内，又能通过将高斯函数相对于目标相机定位并朝向目标场景的光源位置设置，将其锚定到目标场景中。 对于每一帧，我们首先从目标相机视角对目标高斯函数进行光栅化，这也会生成一个逆深度图，用于执行每盏光源的可见性测试：只有未被目标几何体遮挡的目标光源才会实例化光晕效果。 每个可见的目标光源都会生成一个光晕实例，这些实例随后被合并，并与目标渲染结果合成，以确保迁移后的光晕能够正确融入目标场景（并被其遮挡）。 由于光晕会跟随目标相机移动，因此我们沿着目标场景的平滑视频轨迹进行渲染，以生成迁移序列。 由于光晕以高斯函数的形式显式表示，因此在迁移后仍然可以直接编辑：图 14 的最下面一行展示了一个迁移后的光晕效果，其高斯函数被统一缩放为 2 × 2\times，从而无需任何重新训练即可对光晕的表观强度和范围进行简单的艺术性控制。

paragraphs.en: A key practical concern is how sensitive our flare representation is to errors in the input light-source locations. In the wild, Grounded-SAM2 detections can be inconsistent across views or off by tens-to-hundreds of pixels under saturation, motion blur, or occlusion. Any flare model that hard-codes l l as a fixed prior is therefore vulnerable to a noisy front-end. To stress-test our pipeline, we displace each light’s estimated 3D position by a single Gaussian offset of standard deviation σ ∈ { 0.0 , 0.1 , 0.5 , 1.0 } \sigma\in\{0.0,0.1,0.5,1.0\} (in scene units), held fixed for the whole sequence; projected into the views, this corresponds to an average error of up to ∼ 262 \sim\!262 px, on five of our scenes ( chair , hat , metro , outtree , workshop , spanning one to three light sources), and evaluate every combination of our light-position correction δ l \delta_{l} (Eq. ( 6 )) and finer deformations δ f \delta_{f} (Eq. ( 5 )).
paragraphs.zh: 一个关键的实际问题是，我们的光晕表示对输入光源位置中的误差有多敏感。在实际应用中，Grounded-SAM2 的检测结果在不同视角之间可能不一致，或在饱和度、运动模糊或遮挡的情况下出现数十至数百像素的偏差。因此，任何将 l l 硬编码为固定先验的光晕模型都容易受到前端噪声的影响。为了对我們的流程进行压力测试，我们将每个光源的估计 3D 位置沿单个高斯偏移量进行位移，其标准差为 σ ∈ { 0.0 , 0.1 , 0.5 , 1.0 } \sigma\in\{0.0,0.1,0.5,1.0\}（以场景单位为度量），并在整个序列中保持固定；投影到各视角后，这相当于在我们五个场景（chair、hat、metro、outtree、workshop，包含一个至三个光源）中平均误差高达 ∼ 262 \sim\!262 px。我们评估了光源位置修正 δ l \delta_{l}（公式 (6)）与更精细的形变 δ f \delta_{f}（公式 (5)）的所有组合。

paragraphs.en: As shown in Fig. 15 , the composite PSNR of our full model degrades by 1.5 1.5 dB across the full noise range (from 33.82 33.82 to 32.29 32.29 dB at an average light-position error of 262 262 px) and flare PSNR by 1.4 1.4 dB ( 33.48 33.48 to 32.12 32.12 dB). Scene PSNR, omitted from the plot, stays within 0.1 0.1 dB for every variant except the one with both corrections removed, where it drops from 32.19 32.19 to 31.57 31.57 dB: light-position error leaks into the scene only when the flare model cannot absorb it. Removing either correction alone costs little: at the highest noise level the composite reaches 32.04 32.04 dB without δ l \delta_{l} and 31.86 31.86 dB without δ f \delta_{f} . Removing both is what breaks robustness – the composite falls from 32.72 32.72 to 28.24 28.24 dB and flare PSNR from 32.69 32.69 to 27.27 27.27 dB. δ l \delta_{l} and δ f \delta_{f} are therefore largely redundant defences against detection noise: each gives the flare model enough freedom to compensate for a misplaced principal-point line. Fig. 16 shows the same pattern on the hat sequence: with at least one correction, the flare stays centred on the source and keeps its structure through moderate noise, softening only at σ = 1.0 \sigma=1.0 ; with both removed, its starburst is already lost at σ = 0.1 \sigma=0.1 and it collapses to a faint blob by σ = 1.0 \sigma=1.0 . Because each light is displaced once for the whole sequence, the resulting error is consistent across views rather than independent per view, and so cannot be averaged out. Together with the wo G-SAM2 ablation, which discards detection entirely and places every light near the scene centroid, this indicates that our reconstruction tolerates both inaccurate and missing light detections.

sents.en: Because each light is displaced once for the whole sequence, the resulting error is consistent across views rather than independent per view, and so cannot be averaged out.

sents.en: Together with the wo G-SAM2 ablation, which discards detection entirely and places every light near the scene centroid, this indicates that our reconstruction tolerates both inaccurate and missing light detections.

paragraphs.en: Our flare representation model improves 3DGS’s performance in scenes with lens flares by decomposing the scene into a lens-flare component and a flare-free component, enabling many downstream applications such as flare transfer and editing. While our 2D removal model already handles ring-shaped flares (we explicitly include procedurally generated rings in its training set, see Sec. 4 ), their 3D representation remains an open problem: because our flare Gaussians have peak opacity at the mean and decrease radially away from it (see Fig. 17 ), a single Gaussian cannot form the annular profile required for rings. We therefore leave the 3D representation of ring-shaped flares for future work. Further, light sources out of frame are handled based on projected depth, however, those occluded by scene geometry within a captured view are currently handled implicitly through our flare representation model, rather than through an explicit occlusion-aware mechanism; we leave this to future work.

paragraphs.en: We introduced two models: a lens-flare removal model and, to our knowledge, the first lens-flare representation reconstructed from captured multi-view images. We compiled a dataset of full-image lens flares from publicly available real-world data. Further, we evaluated our flare removal models on the established Flare7k++ benchmark and our proposed VFX benchmark, where on each one of our two models outperforms all compared baselines. Moreover, our 2D flare removal model outperforms baselines, even in 3D scenes, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance on our proposed benchmark for consistent flare removal across multiple views. We used flare removal to develop the lens-flare representation model and demonstrated a decomposed reconstruction of a given scene with flares into scene Gaussians and our flare Gaussians. We believe these models would be useful for different downstream tasks and end-user applications.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了两个模型：一个用于去除镜头眩光的模型，以及据我们所知，首个能从已捕获的多视角图像中重建镜头眩光表示的模型。 我们从公开可用的真实世界数据中整理出了一个包含完整图像镜头眩光的数据集。 此外，我们在成熟的 Flare7k++ 基准测试和我们提出的 VFX 基准测试上评估了我们的眩光去除模型，结果表明，我们提出的两个模型在各自测试中都优于所有对比基线模型。 而且，我们的二维眩光去除模型即使在三维场景中也能超越基线模型，证明了我们提出的基准测试中，该模型在跨多视角一致去除眩光方面达到了当前最优性能。 我们利用眩光去除技术开发了镜头眩光表示模型，并展示了对给定含眩光场景进行分解重建的结果，将其分为场景高斯成分和我们的眩光高斯成分。 我们相信这些模型对于不同的下游任务和最终用户应用都会很有用。

paragraphs.en: For each light source, the deformation network is an instant-NGP-style model: the light input (the absolute normalized image-plane offset of the projected light from the principal point, together with its norm) and the camera position are encoded with multiresolution hash grids of 16 16 levels and 2 2 features per level, a base resolution of 16 16 , hash-table sizes of 2 17 2^{17} and 2 15 2^{15} , and per-level scales of 1.8 1.8 and 1.6 1.6 , respectively; the 1D canonical position uses a frequency encoding with 3 3 bands. The result is decoded by an MLP backbone with 3 3 hidden layers of width 128 128 and ReLU activations. Flare Gaussians are placed at a depth of 0.21 0.21 in the camera frame, just beyond the near plane. We optimize the network and encodings with Adam at a learning rate of 10 − 4 10^{-4} . The canonical flare Gaussians use a position learning rate of 1.6 × 10 − 4 1.6\times 10^{-4} , decayed exponentially to 1.6 × 10 − 6 1.6\times 10^{-6} , and learning rates of 2.5 × 10 − 3 2.5\times 10^{-3} , 0.05 0.05 , 0.1 0.1 and 10 − 3 10^{-3} for their features, opacities, scales and rotations, respectively. We train for 30,000 30{,}000 iterations. We initialize 200 200 flare Gaussians at different positions along a line with reasonable sizes, ensuring that they do not occupy the entire image. We clone and prune the flare Gaussians every 500 500 iterations, from 1 ​ k 1k to 12 ​ k 12k iterations. We allow cloning to be aggressive for all opacities above 0.005 0.005 , with a clone ratio of 0.2 0.2 , and perturb cloned Gaussians with Gaussian noise of standard deviation 0.02 0.02 . We only prune Gaussians when the opacity is below 0.002 0.002 . paragraphs.en: Our flare representation relies on Grounded-SAM2 to obtain the initial 2D light-source locations that are aggregated across views and refined by our model (Sec. 3.2 , main). paragraphs.en: We composite real light sources from Flare7K++ ( Dai et al., 2023a ) onto light-free backgrounds from Flickr24K ( Zhang et al., 2018 ) and our captured images ( 1 1 – 5 5 sources per image, random affine transforms), yielding 1,128 1{,}128 images with exact ground-truth masks.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将 Flare7K++（Dai et al., 2023a）中的真实光源合成到来自 Flickr24K（Zhang et al., 2018）和无光背景的图像上，以及我们采集的图像（每幅图像包含 1–5 个光源，并应用随机仿射变换），最终生成 1,128 幅带有精确真值掩码的图像。

paragraphs.en: We compare the union of predicted SAM2 masks against the ground-truth masks at the pixel level (precision, recall, F1, IoU), sweeping GroundingDINO’s box-confidence threshold from 0.05 0.05 to 0.80 0.80 ( Fig. 19 ), since this threshold alone governs the pipeline’s precision–recall trade-off (SAM2 only segments the boxes it is given). The raw pipeline peaks at F1 0.31 0.31 (threshold 0.50 0.50 ): low thresholds yield many spurious boxes, and SAM2 tends to segment the illuminated halo rather than the compact source. Our refinements – resolving overlapping boxes and discarding non-over-exposed detections – substantially improve precision over the raw pipeline, at a small cost in recall at the lowest thresholds, reaching F1 0.66 0.66 (precision 0.51 0.51 , recall 0.93 0.93 , IoU 0.49 0.49 ) at threshold 0.20 0.20 (Fig. 20 ).
paragraphs.zh: 我们在像素级别（精确度、召回率、F1、IoU）将预测的 SAM2 掩码的并集与真实掩码进行比较，同时将 GroundingDINO 的框置信度阈值从 0.05 到 0.80 逐步调整（图 19），因为仅该阈值就决定了整个流程中精确度与召回率之间的权衡（SAM2 只会对其输入的框进行分割）。 原始流程在 F1 为 0.31 时达到峰值（阈值为 0.50）：较低的阈值会产生大量虚假框，而 SAM2 倾向于分割发光的光晕，而非紧凑的源物体。 我们的改进方法——解决重叠框问题并丢弃非过度曝光的检测——显著提升了相对于原始流程的精确度，仅在最低阈值下对召回率造成轻微影响，在阈值为 0.20 时达到 F1 0.66（精确度 0.51，召回率 0.93，IoU 0.49）（图 20）。

paragraphs.en: On our nine captured scenes for flare reconstruction in Sec. 4.2 ( ∼ \sim 10.8K frames: every frame of the videos, rather than only those sampled for training and testing; no ground truth), at the box threshold of 0.35 0.35 used in our pipeline, GroundingDINO proposes 10,526 10{,}526 boxes; the over-exposure filter discards 993 993 ( 9.4 % 9.4\% ) and overlap-resolution a further 499 499 ( 5.2 % 5.2\% of the remainder), leaving 9,034 9{,}034 ( 85.8 % 85.8\% ). Notably, 93.6 % 93.6\% of the overlap-removed boxes fall below the IoU threshold and would survive standard NMS, motivating our containment-based criterion instead. Lowering the threshold to 0.10 0.10 inflates proposals roughly tenfold, of which the refinements prune only ∼ 82 % \sim\!82\% . Detection is also intermittent across frames ( 2,216 2{,}216 frames with no detection, 319 319 fully filtered), which is precisely what our multi-view 3D aggregation with TRASE ( Li et al., 2026 ) resolves, consolidating noisy per-frame 2D detections into a consistent set of 3D light sources per scene.
